mainProgression.description: The iconic riff progression using a minor key descent with the flattened sixth and seventh creating the signature emotional tension

sectionProgressions.description: The instantly recognizable guitar riff featuring dual guitars (Clapton and Allman)
Verse variation resolving to the dominant A chord for forward momentum
Returns to the main progression with vocal melody 'Layla, you got me on my knees'

sectionProgressions.progression: C - C/E - F - F/A - Bb - C - Dm
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: VII - VII - III - III - VI - VII - i
sectionProgressions.description: The famous piano coda section in a contrasting major-leaning progression

harmonicFunction: Dm (i) - The tonic minor key center establishing the song's emotional depth
Bb (VI) - The flattened sixth providing the characteristic minor-key sound
C (VII) - The flattened seventh creating forward motion back to the tonic
A (V) - Dominant chord used in verses for strong harmonic pull
F (III) - Major mediant appearing in the piano coda section

techniques.name: Blues-Rock Riffing (Dual Guitar)
techniques.description: The iconic main riff featuring dual guitar interplay between Eric Claptonthe iconic vocal hooks slide guitar, creating one of rock's most passionate guitar arrangements

notes: Clapton plays the primary riff on standard guitar with aggressive picking
Allman doubles the riff with slide guitar adding a vocal, singing quality
The riff uses D minor pentatonic notes with chromatic passing tones
Tight unison playing between two guitars is essential to the song's power
The riff has a driving, urgent quality that matches the song's emotional intensity
sequence: Begin on the Dm chord position at the 10th fret
Descend through Bb (6th fret) and C (8th fret) shapes
Resolve back to Dm with a strong rhythmic attack
Repeat with increasing intensity through each cycle
tips: Focus on learning Clapton's standard guitar part first before attempting slide
Use aggressive downstrokes for the main riff notes
The riff has a specific rhythmic feel that is slightly ahead of the beat for urgency
Practice with the recording to absorb the dual guitar interplay
details.progression: Dm - Bb - C - Dm (i - VI - VII - i)

techniques.name: Blues Bending and Lead Phrasing
techniques.description: Expressive blues bending and passionate lead phrasing used throughout the solo sections, showcasing Clapton at his most emotionally intense

notes: Clapton's bending here is urgent and emotionally charged
Uses whole-step, half-step, and quarter-tone bends for expression
Phrases are vocal-like, as if the guitar is crying or pleading
D minor pentatonic and blues scale provide the melodic vocabulary
sequence: Position in D minor pentatonic at the 10th or 13th fret box
Execute aggressive whole-step bends on the B and G strings
Combine bends with fast vibrato for emotional intensity
Use pull-offs and hammer-ons for fluid legato passages
tips: Channel emotional intensity into your bending - this is passionate playing
Do not hold back on vibrato width and speed
Practice connecting pentatonic box shapes for melodic movement
Listen to Clapton's phrasing to understand the emotional arc of each solo section
details.progression: Over Dm - Bb - C - Dm progression

techniques.name: Slide Guitar (Duane Allman Style)
techniques.description: Allmanthe iconic vocal hooks parts, adding a singing, vocal quality to the arrangement

notes: Allman used a glass Coricidin bottle as a slide on his ring finger
Slide plays the main riff melody an octave higher for thickness
Precise intonation is critical - the slide must land exactly on the fret positions
Muting behind the slide is essential to avoid unwanted string noise
sequence: Place glass or metal slide on the ring or pinky finger
Position slide directly over the fret wire (not between frets)
Play the main riff melody in the upper register (above 12th fret)
Damp strings behind the slide with trailing fingers
tips: Start learning slide technique on a separate guitar with higher action if possible
Focus on intonation - the slide must be precisely positioned over the fret
Use light touch - do not press the slide into the fretboard
Damping technique with trailing fingers prevents unwanted overtones
details.progression: Doubling the riff melody Dm - Bb - C - Dm

sections.name: Intro Riff
sections.description: The legendary opening riff featuring Clapton and Allman playing in unison and harmony, one of the most instantly recognizable guitar passages in rock history
notes: Dual guitar arrangement is essential - Clapton on standard, Allman on slide
The riff has an urgent, driving quality that sets the emotional tone
Each repetition builds in intensity
Tight rhythmic coordination between both guitar parts

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Verse section with the riff continuing under Clapton's desperate vocal delivery, the guitars pulling back slightly in dynamics to support the singing
notes: Guitars pull back slightly in volume to support vocals
Verse resolves to A chord rather than returning to Dm
Lead fills are more sparse during verse sections
Emotional arc of the lyrics is matched by guitar dynamics

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Chorus section with the iconic the signature vocal hook, guitars return to full intensity with the main riff driving underneath
notes: Full intensity return with the signature vocal hook
Main riff drives the chorus with maximum energy
Lead guitar adds expressive fills between vocal phrases
Emotional peak of the rock section of the song

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Extended dual-guitar solo section with Clapton and Allman trading and interweaving lead lines over the chord progression, showcasing some of the finest blues-rock guitar playing ever recorded
notes: Clapton and Allman trade lead phrases in a call-and-response style
Solo combines both D minor pentatonic and D blues scale
Allman's slide adds a singing, crying quality to his phrases
Widely regarded as one of the greatest guitar duets in rock history

sections.name: Piano Coda
sections.description: The famous piano-led coda section that transforms the song from aggressive blues-rock into a beautiful, melancholic instrumental passage with Allman's soaring slide guitar
notes: Complete mood shift from aggressive rock to gentle, reflective instrumental
Piano (Jim Gordon) carries the main melody with guitar providing fills
Slide guitar (Allman) adds sustained, singing lead lines over the piano
This section alone is nearly four minutes, creating a unique two-part song structure

guitar.pickup: Single coils (Strat) for clarity, humbuckers (Les Paul) for slide warmth

amp.recommended: Fender Champ (cranked to distortion) / Marshall JTM45

effects.distortion: Cranked amp natural overdrive - Clapton used a small Fender Champ turned up to maximum
effects.other: Glass Coricidin bottle slide for Allman's parts, no other pedals used on the original recording

beginner.title: Getting Started with Layla
steps: Learn Dm, Bb, C, and A chord shapes as open and barre chords
Practice the basic chord progression slowly: Dm - Bb - C - Dm
Work on single-note picking on the low strings for the riff melody
Build finger strength for barre chords used in the progression

intermediate.title: Learning the Riff and Rhythm Parts
steps: Master the complete main riff at full tempo (116 BPM)
Develop bending technique in D minor pentatonic
Learn the verse and chorus chord progressions with proper dynamics
Practice transitioning between the rock section and piano coda feel

advanced.title: Dual Guitar and Complete Mastery
steps: Learn both Claptonthe iconic vocal hooks slide parts
Develop slide guitar technique with proper intonation and damping
Master the dual-guitar solo section with proper phrasing
Perform the complete 7-minute song with authentic dynamics and feel

commonMistakes: Not playing the riff with enough urgency and emotional intensity
Rushing the riff instead of locking into the 116 BPM groove
Under-bending notes during lead sections - must reach target pitch
Ignoring the dynamic contrast between the rock section and piano coda
practiceRoutine: Warm up with D minor pentatonic scales across multiple positions
Practice the main riff slowly at 80 BPM, gradually increasing to 116 BPM
Work on bending exercises in D minor pentatonic with vibrato
Practice the chord progression changes with proper timing
Play along with the original recording to absorb the dual-guitar interplay
focusAreas: Main riff accuracy and rhythmic precision at tempo
Blues bending technique with emotional intensity
Dynamic control between rock and coda sections
Slide guitar fundamentals for the Allman parts
metronomeWork: Start the main riff at 80 BPM and gradually work up to 116 BPM
Practice chord changes with quarter-note clicks for precision
Work on lead phrases with eighth-note subdivisions for timing accuracy
Practice the transition from the rock section into the piano coda timing
